newsitem.title: FRANCE: French accounts commission worried about debt.
newsitem.headline: French accounts commission worried about debt.

text.p: The French national accounts commission said on Monday it was concerned about the rapid growth of French public debt in 1995.
In its report on the implementation of the 1995 budget the Commission said the ongoing rise in debt charges, up by 10.8 percent in 1995, "was one of the most worrying aspects."
"Net debt charges, which amounted to 10.6 percent of net fiscal receipts in 1990, accounted for 15.8 percent of those receipts in 1995," the Commission said in its report.

Outstanding public debt rose to 3.255 billion francs at the end of 1995 compared with 2.904 billion at the end of 1994 with debt charges rose to 452.6 billion from 357.1 billion in 1994, the report said.
As a percentage of gross domestic product, outstanding debt rose 12 percent to 52.2 percent. During the period from 1992 to 1995, it rose 1.129 billion francs, or 58.4 percent the report said.
"Our country is quickly approaching the 60 percent ceiling fixed by the Maastricht Treaty," Pierre Joxe, head of the national accounts commission told a news conference on Monday.
